channel.title: California Uzbek — Latest
channel.description: Independent analysis · Central Asia & world geopolitics

item.title: How to Send Money to Uzbekistan From Abroad: Methods, Costs and Rules
item.description: A practical reference based on the World Bank's Remittance Prices Worldwide reports, Central Bank of Uzbekistan data and reputable news sources. It explains the main transfer methods, the true cost (fee plus exchange-rate margin), speed, receiving rules and safety tips. This is informational, not financial advice.

item.title: Tajikistan turns to Iran for oil as Russia's fuel crisis deepens
item.description: Dushanbe has requested a total of 2.55 million tonnes of oil and fuel from Iran. It is an emergency hedge against Russia's fuel shortage — but it risks US secondary sanctions.

item.title: Uzbekistan's gas exports fell 35% while imports rose 15%
item.description: According to the Statistics Agency, gas exports dropped to $322.3 million in January–August 2026 while imports climbed to $1.22 billion. The country has been a net gas importer since 2023.

item.title: Sea Breeze Uzbekistan: Charvak resort clears second stage of environmental review
item.description: According to Times of Central Asia, the 577-hectare project on the Charvak shore has passed the first two environmental stages. A final assessment is required after construction.

item.title: US Temporary Work Visas: How H-1B, H-2A and H-2B Work
item.description: A reference guide based on the official pages of U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), the Department of Labor (DOL) and the Department of State (travel.state.gov). It explains how the H-1B visa for specialty occupations, the H-2A visa for seasonal agricultural work and the H-2B visa for temporary non-agricultural work operate, the application process and the key rules. This is informational, not legal advice.

item.title: The Uzbek Diaspora in Kazakhstan: How the Southern Community Took Shape
item.description: A fact-based article on the historical formation of the Uzbek community living in southern Kazakhstan — the Turkistan Region, Shymkent and along the Syr Darya. It traces the period from the Kokand Khanate through the drawing of Soviet state borders to the present-day population in independent Kazakhstan, with dates and figures. Verified facts only.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Defence Ministry inspection leads to 13 criminal cases after 14 soldiers die
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev ordered a sweeping inspection after the 24 September Caspian tragedy. The result: 13 criminal cases, a change of minister and a two-year military reform.

item.title: The 'Mecca Pact' is activated for the first time: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Türkiye against the Houthis
item.description: The three-nation collective-defence pact signed on 7 August was activated in Riyadh on 5 October. Meanwhile, a Saudi-led coalition has launched an operation in Yemen.

item.title: Strait of Hormuz: oil exports top pre-war levels despite Iran's closure claims
item.description: According to Kpler and Vortexa, Middle East oil exports returned in September to a pre-war level of about 18 million barrels a day — even as attacks on tankers escalate.

item.title: Industrial AI is reaching Kazakhstan's factories and mines, but many projects remain experimental
item.description: A 2025–26 government roadmap covers 41 projects at 11 major enterprises. ERG's autonomous haul trucks have already moved more than two million tonnes of rock.

item.title: World's largest AI film festival concludes in Astana, with the Grand Prix going to Latvia
item.description: The festival drew 8,067 entries from 125 countries; its $450,000 Grand Prix went to Latvian filmmaker Nikolay Shestak's 'The First Honest Day.'

item.title: How to Protect Yourself From Fraud and Scams in the USA: the Traps That Target Immigrants
item.description: A reference guide grounded in official guidance from the Federal Trade Commission (FTC), the IRS, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), and the Social Security Administration (SSA). It explains government-impersonation calls, immigration and tax fraud, tech-support and phishing traps, and the payment red flags — how to spot them and where to report. This is a reference, not legal advice.

item.title: From Plan to Market: Uzbekistan's Early Years of Economic Reform (1991–1996)
item.description: After Uzbekistan declared independence on 31 August 1991, the transition from the Soviet planned economy toward a market economy began. Between 1991 and 1996 came gradual privatization, partial price liberalization, the introduction of the national currency — the som — and membership of international financial institutions such as the IMF and the World Bank. The documented dates and figures are set out below.

item.title: Uzbekistan as a Wartime Refuge: Evacuation and Deportation, 1941–1945
item.description: Between 1941 and 1945 Uzbekistan lived through one of the heaviest and most layered chapters of its migration history. On one side, hundreds of thousands of people, children, factories and institutions evacuated from the war zones; on the other, the forced deportation of entire peoples to the Uzbek SSR under Stalin. This article relies only on verified dates and figures; where sources disagree, a range is given.

item.title: Buying a car in the USA: auto loan, insurance, and total cost — a practical reference for immigrants
item.description: How buying a car works in the USA: new vs used, dealer vs private seller, the auto loan (APR, term, down payment), insurance, and total cost of ownership. Official sources: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB), Federal Trade Commission (FTC), the Insurance Information Institute (III), and the California DMV. This is a reference, not financial advice.

item.title: Central Asian leaders and Azerbaijan to hold first formal summit in Avaza on October 8
item.description: Six heads of state will meet at Turkmenistan's Caspian resort of Avaza — the first formal summit since Azerbaijan became a full member of the format in November 2025.

item.title: Palestinian Education Ministry: more than 800 teachers killed in Gaza since the war began
item.description: Ahead of World Teachers' Day, the ministry says more than 800 teachers and education staff have been killed since October 7, 2023, over 3,300 injured and more than 170 detained. The figures are the ministry's count; Israel disputes some tallies.

item.title: Uzbek migration to Turkey: from historical roots to the modern community
item.description: In recent decades Turkey has become a major destination for Uzbeks. Below, the historical roots of the Turkestani émigrés, the 2018 visa-free regime, Turkey's migration-service figures on residence permits, the neighborhood restrictions and the 2026 labor agreement are set out using only verified sources.

item.title: Uzbekistan finishes fifth at the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games with 70 medals
item.description: Uzbekistan won 21 gold, 25 silver and 24 bronze to place fifth overall. Central Asia's five states together collected 186 medals.

item.title: The revival of Amir Temur's legacy in independent Uzbekistan (1991–1996)
item.description: After independence, Uzbekistan began honoring Amir Temur as a national hero. Below, the unveiling of the Amir Temur statue in Tashkent (1994), the State Museum of the History of the Temurids (1996), the 660th anniversary in 1996 and other facts are set out with exact dates, using only verified sources.

item.title: Starting a small business in the US: LLC, EIN and tax basics
item.description: In the US, the most common way to run a small business is to form an LLC (a limited liability company) and get an EIN (a federal tax number) from the IRS. Below, business structures, how an LLC is registered, how an EIN is obtained (for free), how tax works and the rules for non-citizens are explained using official sources — the SBA and the IRS. This is a reference, not legal advice.

item.title: Zelensky: the US wants a trilateral US–Ukraine–Russia meeting by the end of October
item.description: After meeting German Chancellor Friedrich Merz in Kyiv, Zelensky said the US side is proposing a technical-level trilateral meeting by the end of October. Merz announced about €1 billion in military aid.

item.title: Russia vows to step up strikes; Ukraine to retaliate against Russian oil refineries
item.description: Russia's Defense Ministry said it would intensify strikes, while President Volodymyr Zelensky vowed to increase attacks on Russian oil refineries. Ukrainian drones have struck refineries about 70 times in 2026.

item.title: How buying a home and a mortgage work in the US: the basics for immigrants
item.description: In the US, the main way to buy a home is a mortgage. Below, how a mortgage works, the down payment and PMI, the role of your credit score, FHA loans, closing costs and the options for immigrants (green-card and work-visa holders) are explained using only official sources — CFPB, FHA/HUD and Fannie Mae. This is a reference, not financial advice.

item.title: CAIR urges White House and Congress to demand release of US citizen Abdalkareem Safi held by Israel
item.description: The Council on American-Islamic Relations says 19-year-old US citizen Abdalkareem Issa Ahmed Safi has been held by Israel without charge in administrative detention since June, and called on the State Department to secure his release.

item.title: G7 to release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel to curb prices
item.description: The G7 and EU will release up to 100 million barrels of oil and diesel reserves over four months — diesel frontloaded in the first 20 days — to ease fuel prices driven up by the wars on Iran and in Ukraine.

item.title: The Cotton Affair (the 'Uzbek affair'): the 1980s investigation and its consequences
item.description: The 'Cotton Affair', also called the 'Uzbek affair', was a major Soviet-era criminal investigation into the padding of cotton figures (pripiski) and corruption in Uzbekistan's cotton economy in the 1980s. It led to some 800 criminal cases and more than 4,000 people found guilty. Below, its causes, scale and consequences are set out using only verified sources.

item.title: Strike on a Gaza City apartment building kills at least five Palestinians
item.description: Palestinian health and civil-defence officials say an early-Saturday Israeli strike on a residential building in Gaza City killed at least five people, four of them women, as the ceasefire holds only on paper.

item.title: Kazakhstan plans a fourth major oil refinery by 2033
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Energy plans to commission a new refinery with capacity of up to 10 million tonnes a year by 2033 and to choose its location by the end of 2026.

item.title: How the Qurbani (Eid al-Adha sacrifice) is performed: rules, conditions and meaning
item.description: Qurbani (Arabic: udhiyah) is the sacrifice of a designated animal for the sake of God on the days of Eid al-Adha. It commemorates the story of Prophet Ibrahim. Below, when and on whom it is due, which animals qualify, how the meat is distributed and the differences between the schools are explained using broadly accepted sources, primarily the Hanafi school.
